purpose: Record primary-source findings about mid-training, SFT, distillation, RL and reasoning-budget control, then translate them into bounded experiments for a small data-centered release.
scope: On-policy distillation and DAPO-style length control

claims: The 1B and 2B recipes use base training, capability mid-training, SFT, specialist RL and on-policy distillation.
Specialist teachers cover reasoning, coding, knowledge, writing and agent tasks before capabilities are merged into one checkpoint.
The release reports a two-stage reasoning length schedule and fewer max-token hits after RL plus OPD.
Post-training separates reasoning RL, thinking-mode fusion and general RL.
The report evaluates explicit thinking and non-thinking modes and a thinking-budget mechanism.
On-policy distillation reaches the reported 8B result with roughly one tenth of the RL GPU-hours in that comparison.
Expert SFT creates reasoning, agent and general-chat specialists; unified SFT self-distills them into a hybrid model.
The data mixes full reasoning with direct responses so short tasks do not pay an unnecessary reasoning cost.
Rejection sampling checks correctness, repetition, truncation and reasoning validity before training.
K2 synthesizes multi-turn tool trajectories and combines verifiable rewards with self-critique rubric rewards.
Its RL inventory spans math, STEM, instruction following, faithfulness, coding, software engineering and safety.
The technical report includes explicit budget control, PTX loss and temperature scheduling as RL concerns.
A length penalty is warmed up instead of applied at full strength from the first update.
Cold-start reasoning SFT improves readability and behavior before RL.
Curated distillation is a strong small-model baseline and is reported to outperform direct small-model RL in the tested comparisons.
Teachable prompt selection and teacher-generated demonstrations are used for reasoning SFT.
A short outcome-based RL phase improves a reasoning checkpoint, showing that RL is a finisher after useful SFT rather than a substitute for it.
The open model flow exposes mid-training, SFT, preference optimization and RLVR checkpoints and datasets.
Separate reasoning SFT, preference and RL data makes stage-specific ablations possible.
A compact model uses a dedicated mid-training reasoning mixture and separately curated post-training data.
The release emphasizes open data and intermediate checkpoints, useful for measuring stage value rather than only final quality.
Post-training combines SFT, GRPO, DPO and RLHF in an efficiency-oriented reasoning model.
The report evaluates budget control and truncation training for long reasoning outputs.
On-policy distillation samples student trajectories and provides dense per-token teacher feedback.
It targets the exposure-bias weakness of off-policy SFT while avoiding the sparse signal of sequence-level RL.
The reported method uses reverse-KL token advantages and can reuse short or partial student rollouts.
Soft overlong punishment creates a graded penalty near the limit instead of treating every truncated response as simply incorrect.
Overlong filtering and token-level accounting reduce reward noise in long-chain RL.

common_post_training_shape: reasoning and agent SFT or distillation
general capability repair and policy unification
on-policy distillation or replay to recover earlier skills

data_banks.purpose: Instruction following, factual answers, writing, multilingual coverage and safe conversational behavior.
data_banks.required_evidence: Independent protocol, factuality and held-out-family checks.

data_banks.purpose: Teacher-generated or curated math, code, science and planning traces with final-answer correctness.
data_banks.required_evidence: Answer verification, reasoning/final separation, repetition and truncation checks.

data_banks.purpose: Complete tool trajectories with valid schemas, observations, recovery and final outcomes.
data_banks.required_evidence: Replay in the declared environment; teacher claims alone are insufficient.

data_banks.purpose: Prompts with independent references, tests or rubrics for on-policy learning.
data_banks.required_evidence: Verifier validity, difficulty strata, wrong-answer controls and environment recovery cost.

data_banks.purpose: Pairwise or rubric feedback for style, safety, instruction following and non-verifiable quality.
data_banks.required_evidence: Judge agreement, calibration, adversarial checks and contamination controls.

data_banks.purpose: Dense teacher scores on student-visited states for exposure-bias reduction and capability repair.
data_banks.required_evidence: Teacher cost, per-token coverage, teacher/student identity and regression checks.

synthesis.small_model_priority: For a 1.2B-class model, establish useful behavior with verified SFT or distillation before policy optimization. Use RL only where the reward is independently checkable and where fixed-policy feasibility shows enough signal to justify updates.
what_transfers: Stage separation and explicit lineage transfer directly.
Specialist data banks are more actionable than a single undifferentiated post-training mixture.
Outcome verification, on-policy coverage and cost accounting should be first-class measurements.
General capability repair is needed after specialized mid-training or RL to limit regressions.
what_does_not_transfer: Published token counts, teacher sizes, model ratios and GPU-hours are not portable to Speck.
A frontier lab's rubric or reward model is not evidence that our local verifier is valid.
A supported chat-template switch does not prove that a new small model will learn reliable budget control.
Reported benchmark gains do not establish broad assistant quality or tool reliability.

reasoning_control_decision.default_release_policy: Keep the current always-thinking contract as the release baseline until a controlled study shows that a hybrid policy improves quality-cost tradeoffs without mode or format regressions.
hypotheses: A trained think/no-think switch can reduce latency on simple tasks, but a prompt or template flag may create mode confusion if the training distribution is too small or inconsistent.
A continuous token cap is an inference truncation control; it is not evidence that the model learned a useful low, medium or high reasoning policy.
A small set of discrete budget buckets may be learnable when each bucket has explicit supervision and task-matched outcomes, but rigid caps can cause premature truncation or length overfitting.

conditions: hybrid think/no-think only if training data contains both modes with explicit labels
three task-matched budget buckets recorded as requested and actual reasoning tokens
metrics: correctness and tool success at matched task families
quality per generated token and per wall-clock/GPU cost
format, mode-switch, truncation and regression rates
bounded_experiment.promotion_rule: Do not expose low/medium/high controls in the release interface unless all buckets beat or match the always-thinking baseline on their intended cost-quality frontier and pass held-out mode-following tests.
bounded_experiment.boundary: No new training arm or GPU-hours are created by this artifact. The first executable check is evaluation or fixed-policy feasibility on an already useful SFT parent.

rl_length_efficiency.decision: Optimize correctness first and efficiency second. Do not use a global shortness reward that can make the model guess, omit verification or truncate valid reasoning.
reward_order: invalid or unsafe tool behavior is rejected
independent task outcome or verifier correctness is the primary signal
only correct or otherwise admissible responses receive an efficiency preference
length cost is task-conditioned and applied softly near a declared budget
recommended_measurement: quality-versus-reasoning-token Pareto curves by task family
success per generated token and per rollout GPU-hour
truncation, repetition, shortcut and verifier-hacking rates
difficulty-normalized length, not one global token target
performance after increasing the inference budget beyond the training budget
training_guardrails: warm up or delay any length penalty
use a soft overlong zone and mask ambiguous truncations from the main update
keep a correctness floor and a general-capability replay stream
report separate reasoning, tool-observation and final-answer tokens
compare fixed-policy rollouts before policy updates
failure_modes: premature stop at a learned cap
hidden reasoning moved into the final answer
verifier exploitation or reward-model style gaming
long-task regressions caused by a budget trained on easy tasks

speck_actions: Keep the existing two-arm SFT selection study and add this artifact to its evidence index.
Retain the fixed-policy RL feasibility slot; add length, verifier and recovery measurements before any policy update.
Prepare separate general, reasoning, agent, verifier, preference and on-policy-feedback manifests under the shared data-design contract.
Use a useful SFT parent for the first reasoning-control check; do not change the always-thinking release contract from a literature claim.
If the feasibility evidence is positive, run one small correctness-first length-efficiency ablation before broad RL.
Keep teacher generation, verifier execution, rejected rows, rollouts and policy updates in separate cost ledgers.
boundary: This review changes the post-training research questions and audit outputs, not source admission, model architecture, production token counts or the 5,000-GPU-hour envelope.
